Cast: Scarlett Johansson, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Diane Lane, Jacobi Jupe, Sasha  Calle, Scoot McNairy, Gil Bellows with Laurence Fishburne and John Leguizamo 

Academy Award®️ nominee Scarlett Johansson fronts The Exorcist: Martyrs, an unsettling new chapter in one of the most storied titles in cinema history from genre auteur Mike Flanagan, the creator of  acclaimed series The Haunting of Hill House, The Fall of the House of Usher, Midnight Mass, and the  upcoming Carrie, as well as the films Doctor Sleep, The Life of Chuck, Hush and Gerald’s Game. 

Thirteen years ago, New York City detective Julie Miller (Johansson) ended the terror reign of satanic serial killer Father Sunday. The case made her a hero, and she has thrown herself into her work ever since. Now a new killer scrawls her name in an altar boy’s blood on the walls of a church crypt, dragging her back into the darkness she believed she had buried with him.  

Aided by former prison chaplain Father William (Academy Award®️ nominee Chiwetel Ejiofor), who heard Father Sunday’s final confession, and sharp rookie detective Gina Restrepo (Sasha Calle, The Rip), Detective Miller will discover a filament linking a lineage of serial killers, from H.H. Holmes to the Zodiac, that could corrupt everything, and everyone, she loves with an evil that goes well beyond the mortal.  

The top-flight cast includes Academy Award®️ nominee Diane Lane as Mary, Detective Miller’s mother, who has moved in with her to help raise her grandson Max (Jacobi Jupe, Hamnet); Actor Award winner Scoot McNairy (Argo) as paroled convict Clay Silver; Emmy winner Gil Bellows (Carrie) as Peter Nicks, a former acolyte of Father Sunday; Emmy and Tony winning screen legend Laurence Fishburne as revered priest Father Nichol; and acclaimed star of The Odyssey, Emmy and Special Tony Award winner John Leguizamo, in the most menacing role of his career as Father Sunday.

The Exorcist: Martyrs is written and directed by Mike Flanagan, based on characters created by William Peter Blatty. The film is produced by David Robinson (The Exorcist series, Dead Ringers series), three time Academy Award®️ nominee Jason Blum (Get Out, Black Phone films) and Mike Flanagan. The film is executive produced by Alexandra Magistro and Ryan Turek.

Track Name: Bombay Ki Rani
Singer, Composer, Lyrics: Nishant Mukta

Lyrics:

VERSE 1
Nasha tohar gajab bate
Ada tohar alag lage
Heroine ke figure bate
Pura Bombay ke khabar bate

Hinglish Translation:
Tumhara nasha bada gajab ka hai.
Tumhari ada sabse alag aur anokhi lagti hai.
Tumhara figure bilkul kisi heroine jaisa hai.
Pure Bombay me bas tumhari hi charcha (khabar) ho rahi hai.

CHORUS
Sapna me je dekhni uhe kahani lagelu
Goriya tu Bombay ke rani lagelu
Goriya tu Bombay ke rani lagelu
Kabho nahi ghate je jawani lagelu
Goriya tu Bombay ke Bombay ke Bombay ke

Hinglish Translation:
Jo tumhe sapno me dekhe, use tum kisi kahani jaisi lagti ho.
Gori ladki, tum toh Bombay ki rani jaisi lagti ho.
Gori ladki, tum toh Bombay ki rani jaisi lagti ho.
Tumhari jawani aisi hai jo kabhi kam (dhal) hi nahi hoti.
Gori ladki, tum toh sach me Bombay ki rani lagti ho.

VERSE 2
Dhoop me nikalna na gori tan ho jayi
Kahi na Nishant toharo fan ho jayi

Hinglish Translation:
Gori ladki, tum Bombay ki rani lagti ho.
Dhoop me mat nikla karo gori, nahi toh rang sanwla (tan) ho jayega.
Kahi Nishant bhi tumhara fan (deewana) na ban jaye.



Dekhila je tohke ham bechain ho jayin
Saans bharal gori na kahin ban ho jayi
Bharal jawani me gori pani me tu aag lagawelu
Rahelu Bombay gori, Patna me tu maar fasawelu

Hinglish Translation:
Jab bhi hum tumhe dekhte hain, bechain ho jaate hain.
Darr lagta hai ki kahin hamari saansein hi na ruk jayein.
Is khilti jawani me gori tum paani me bhi aag laga deti ho.
Rahti toh Bombay me ho gori, par hungama aur kangle-aam Patna me machati ho.

Pahinke LV, Gucci, Prada sbke brand dikhabelu
Nikallu hot je banke, Bandra me jaam laga dehlu

Hinglish Translation:
LV, Gucci aur Prada jaise bade brands pehan kar sabko style dikhati ho.
Jab tum itni hot ban kar nikalti ho, toh Bandra me traffic jam laga deti ho.

RAP
Neeli neeli akhiyan se jadu karelu
Hamra ke kahe bekabu karelu
Dil kare jor se dhak dhak dhak dhak dhak
Nishantwa ke babu kahelu

Are nazari se nazari milaike 
Rakha hamra k pas bulaike 
Tohre se karab biyah ae janu
Boldeni ham apan mai ke 
Bol deni ja

Hinglish Translation:
Apni neeli-neeli aankhon se tum jaadu karti ho.
Hame is tarah apne vash me (bekabu) kyu kar rahi ho?
Mera dil bahut zor-zor se dhak-dhak dhadakne lagta hai.
Jab tum Nishant ko pyaar se 'babu' kahkar bulati ho.
Tumne toh pyaar ka aisa rog laga diya hai.
Aakhon me aakhen dal kar mujhe apne pas baithakar rakho.
Tumse he shadi karunga apni maa ko bol chuka hu.      


VERSE 3
Lagailu ishq ke rog
Jagal rahi roj goriya
Ki ab har raat jaag kar hi beet-ti hai, gori.
Ham na manab hamke chahi love ke dose goriya
Dekhni Insta pe tor model wala pose goriya
Ki man karata ki kardi propose goriya
Bhaiya Ravi ke tu deewani lagelu
Goriya tu Bombay ke rani lagelu


Hinglish Translation:
Ab hum nahi maanenge, hame toh tumhare pyaar ki dose chahiye, gori.
Instagram pe humne tumhara model wala pose dekha hai, gori.
Usko dekh kar dil karta hai ki tumhe seedha propose kar dein, gori.
Tum toh Ravi bhaiya ki deewani lagti ho.
Gori ladki, tum toh Bombay ki rani lagti ho

If you are looking for a comedy short film and family entertainer set against the backdrop of this ritualistic period, you are likely referring to the widely-trending sketches and 3D animated comedy shorts that surface during this season.
Because Pitru Paksha is traditionally a solemn period for honoring ancestors, comedy creators use the unique, everyday cultural quirks of Indian families during these 16 days to create hilarious, lighthearted family entertainment.
Here is a general description of what these highly popular Pitru Paksha comedy family short films entail:

🎬 Typical Plot & Setting

The story usually revolves around a traditional middle-class Indian household trying to strictly follow the rules of Shradh (ancestral rituals). The comedy stems from the generational gap between tech-savvy, modern kids and superstitious or strict elders who are anxious about making a mistake.
